rows.why: We expect about 8.4 carries vs the 12.5 line. We give the under 63% (needs 56% per pick on Underdog); recent games and the matchup both point lower
rows.why_long: Underdog lower 12.5 needs 56% per pick for your entry; fair view 62% (draftkings 11.5, moved to this line). Averaging 10.8 over the last 8 games, lower than 12.5 in 52% of them (raw 56%, shrunk 61%). Projects 8.4 (raw 70%, shrunk 63%).
why_points: The pick: Carries lower 12.5 on Underdog. Each pick has to win 56% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (draftkings 11.5, moved to this line) is 62%.
Other apps: PrizePicks 11. This is the best number for the lower side.
Game log, most recent first: 7, 2, 15, 4, 15, 19, 21, 22. Weighted average 10.8; went lower than 12.5 in 3 of 8 games (52% recency-weighted).
Trending down: last 3 games average 8.0 vs 16.2 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±7.0, so the line is 0.2 of those swings above his average (standard deviations) — basically a coin flip.
Projection: we expect 8.4 carries on average; in a typical game 7.2 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 5.3 below the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 56% and the matchup 70%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 61%, matchup 63%.
Bottom line: we give it 63% to win and it needs 56%. The edge is the difference: +7.0 points; that works out to about +12¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
rows.glance_head: The under looks good: we expect about 7.2 in a typical game vs the 12.5 line, and his recent games and the matchup agree.
